subject: Post-demo: Pilot charter & evaluation plan for AuroraEdge
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Parker <dparker@auroraedge.ai>, Liam Chen <liam.chen@auroraedge.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed 4-week pilot charter

Hi Danielle / Liam —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a concrete pilot proposal to keep momentum. Short version up top, details below.

TL;DR: Redwood proposes a focused 4-week pilot to validate AuroraEdge's three top priorities: latency under 120ms p95 for 512-token requests, semantic search relevance > 0.78 (NDCG@10) on your test set, and <= $0.10 per 1k generated token at target throughput. We’ll provide a sandboxed environment, short-term dedicated capacity, and a compact eval plan. Attached: pilot-charter-draft.pdf (first pass).

Demo highlights (what you told us):
- Primary use case: in-product assistance for customer support agents (short form & retrieval-augmented responses)
- Traffic shape: spikey business hours, avg 12 req/s, peak 45 req/s
- Data constraints: PII redaction needed, customer-owned logs must stay within AuroraEdge-controlled S3

Proposed pilot (4 weeks) — goals and success criteria:
1) Latency & stability (owner: Jonas Weber)
   - p95 latency <= 120ms for 512-token prompt-response in your west-us region
   - <1% failed requests attributable to runtime errors
2) Quality (owner: Marissa Cole)
   - NDCG@10 >= 0.78 on your curated eval set (we’ll provide eval harness and sample prompts)
   - Manual review: >= 85% acceptable response rate across 200 sampled conversations
3) Cost & throughput (owner: Kimberly Park)
   - Average token cost <= $0.10 / 1k generated tokens at sustained 10 req/s
   - Throughput target: sustain 40 req/s for 10-minute windows without SLA breach

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize pilot charter, sign MPA (minimal pilot agreement), grant access to sandbox S3, setup cross-account role
- Week 1: ingest eval set, baseline runs, initial tuning & quantization profile suggested
- Week 2: mid-pilot quality check, perf tuning, cost optimizations, gating review
- Week 3: extended load test, edge-case sampling, security checklist walkthrough
- Week 4: run final eval, wrap report, decision meeting (go/no-go)

Immediate asks from AuroraEdge:
- Confirm which data store you want to use for logs (cross-account S3 vs. SFTP)
- Point of contact for security questionnaire (SOC2 / audit)
- Narrow list of 200 sample conversations for the manual review

Attachments: pilot-charter-draft.pdf (outline above), auroraedge-reqs.xlsx (raw traffic and sample data layout)

Next steps: If this looks good I’ll share an updated charter with dates and a DocuSign link for the MPA — can we aim to kick off next Monday (Mar 23)?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

---

From: Danielle Parker <dparker@auroraedge.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam Chen <liam.chen@auroraedge.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed 4-week pilot charter

Thanks Kim — appreciate the crisp summary. A few quick clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

1) Data access & residency: we prefer cross-account S3 with AuroraEdge-managed buckets (no network egress to third-party storage). Can Redwood support an IAM role approach and only read from our bucket?
2) Compliance lead: I’ll loop in our security manager (cc’d Liam) but want to confirm Redwood’s SOC2 type II status and whether you can provide the standard evidence bundle during the pilot phase.
3) Evaluation set: the 200-sample sounds good. We’ll extract and deliver a de-identified sample by Monday morning.

Two ask from us: can Redwood commit to a __temporary__ reduced token price for the pilot (discounted rate) and provide guidance on expected instrumentation overhead (tokens added by retrieval + system messages)? Also, we’re expecting a procurement contact to handle the MPA — I’ll forward their info shortly.

On dates: Monday (Mar 23) works for a kickoff at 10:00am PT if that aligns with your team.

Cheers,
Danielle Parker
Head of Product | AuroraEdge
Danielle.Parker@auroraedge.ai

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Parker <dparker@auroraedge.ai>, Liam Chen <liam.chen@auroraedge.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed 4-week pilot charter

Danielle — thanks, great questions. Quick answers and next steps below.

Data access: yes — we can use a cross-account read-only IAM role into AuroraEdge-managed S3. We will not copy data outside your account; logs for the pilot can be configured to write to a dedicated, short-lived bucket you control.

Compliance: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified; I’ve attached the SOC2 summary and we can provide the auditor evidence bundle once we have an NDA/MPA in place. Internal contact for compliance: Jonas Weber (cc).

Pricing: we can offer a pilot credit and a provisional 30% discount on standard token rates for the duration of the 4-week pilot — final pricing to be captured in the MPA/quote. We’ll also instrument token accounting in the eval harness so you can see retrieval+prompt overhead.

Procurement: please send your procurement contact and I’ll route the MPA and a short SOW. For speed, we can do the MPA signature electronically.

Kickoff: 10:00am PT on Mon, Mar 23 works for us. I’ll put a calendar invite out after we finalize the MPA.

Updated attachments: I’ve attached pilot-charter-draft.pdf (v1.1) with owners, and auroraedge-reqs.xlsx containing our suggested data mapping.

Owners & immediate internal next actions:
- Jonas Weber: environment & infra (cross-account role, sandbox, perf knobs)
- Marissa Cole: eval harness, NDCG baseline runs, manual review plan
- Kimberly Park: commercial terms, kickoff scheduling, procurement coordination

Next steps for AuroraEdge:
- Send procurement contact + the de-identified 200-sample by Monday morning
- Confirm bucket name and cross-account role owner

Let me know if you want us to prep specific load profiles for the extended test (e.g., 40 req/s for 10m bursts).

Best,
Kimberly

Attachments: pilot-charter-draft.pdf (v1.1), auroraedge-reqs.xlsx

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Parker <dparker@auroraedge.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed 4-week pilot charter — evaluation details

Hi Danielle — quick note on the evaluation mechanics so expectations are aligned:

Quality checks:
- We’ll run an automatic NDCG pipeline on your de-identified test set and post the daily score to the shared drive. NDCG uses your relevance labels; if you don’t have labels for a subset we’ll propose a small labeling pass (approx 2 hours of work).
- Manual review will be randomized sampling of 200 conversations across the pilot. We’ll share a Google Sheet with reviewer judgments (Accept / Partial / Reject) and reasoning tags.

Instrumentation & metrics:
- Token accounting: separate columns for prompt tokens, retrieval tokens, completion tokens.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 by endpoint and model variant; we’ll also surface tail errors with sample payloads for debugging.

Acceptance gate: final go/no-go will be based on the three pillars Kim outlined (latency, quality, cost) after we run the Week 4 final eval and review session.

Happy to walk through the eval harness during kickoff.

Thanks,
Marissa
Lead Applied ML | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

All set on infra from our side. I’ll provision a sandbox cluster in west-us and pre-warm the model variants we discussed so we can hit your burst targets. Also confirming we can support cross-account S3 read-only and will supply an access playbook in the invite.

On the pricing side, I’ll flag a short pilot credit to the commerce team so you see the discounted invoice (internal note: RDW cover up to $6k in pilot usage).
